name: pytrends-modern
what_it_holds: Newer Python client billed as 'combining the best features from pytrends, trendspyg, and more' — a post-archival successor client for the same Google Trends endpoints (interest over time/region, related queries).
why_useful: Alternative maintained client if trendspyg has issues; low incremental value beyond trendspyg since it targets the same underlying data we've already tested.
duplicate_of_holding: Yes — same underlying Trends data already tested and found not useful as pulled.
themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos
why_all: Alternative maintained client if trendspyg has issues; low incremental value beyond trendspyg since it targets the same underlying data we've already tested.

name: gogtrends

why_useful: No incremental data value for this team's Python/R stack; noted only for completeness.

themes: Google Trends tooling and datasets: pytrends, gtab anchored trends, historical trends archives, trends nowcasting repos

name: radar-rs
what_it_holds: Unofficial Rust SDK/client wrapper for the Cloudflare Radar API (BGP routing stats, attack data, DNS, HTTP traffic metrics, bot-traffic breakdowns, top ASNs). Read-only client, requires the user's own Cloudflare API token; commits no data itself.
why_useful: Lower-friction way to pull Cloudflare Radar's HTTP-traffic-by-category and bot/crawler-traffic-share endpoints (which include an internet-traffic-by-industry breakdown covering 'Internet & Telecom'/travel-adjacent categories and AI-bot vs human traffic share) programmatically, relevant to gap 19 (AI-referral / bot crawler share). Requires a free Cloudflare account/API token (not a paid key), so within the 'no paid API keys' rule, but is a thin client rather than a dataset.
time_coverage: live API, no historical bulk export
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)
wildcard: a hedge-fund alternative-data buyer who has seen every vendo
wildcard: a quant building a KPI nowcast for a consumer-internet compa
why_all: Lower-friction way to pull Cloudflare Radar's HTTP-traffic-by-category and bot/crawler-traffic-share endpoints (which include an internet-traffic-by-industry breakdown covering 'Internet & Telecom'/travel-adjacent categories and AI-bot vs human traffic share) programmatically, relevant to gap 19 (AI-referral / bot crawler share). Requires a free Cloudflare account/API token (not a paid key), so within the 'no paid API keys' rule, but is a thin client rather than a dataset.

A code-level client for the same Cloudflare Radar data referenced in gaps #5 and #19; useful once someone registers a free Cloudflare Radar API token to pull historical internet-traffic and AI-bot-share series as an engagement/AI-disintermediation proxy for travel-booking sites broadly.

Another thin client for Radar's traffic-rank and outage endpoints (gap #5/#19: web-traffic-estimate style engagement proxies and bot/AI traffic); low value on its own since it is an unofficial low-star wrapper, but confirms Radar's API is the right target and is scriptable outside Rust via its plain REST endpoints too.

name: ai-visibility-readiness
what_it_holds: Open-source 'AI Visibility Readiness' audit methodology: deterministic HTTP/HTML probes plus live citation measurement, with Cloudflare Radar crawler baselines used to benchmark how much of a site's traffic is AI-bot crawlers vs human. Auto-generates a CHECKS.md from the audit code; framework, not a pre-collected panel.
why_useful: A candidate method (not data) for measuring how 'AI-crawlable'/AI-referenced a given site is, tying to gap 19's LLM-travel-agent-benchmark angle — could in principle be pointed at airbnb.com or competitor booking sites to get an AI-crawler-traffic baseline, though this would count as scraping and needs a human ToS call per repo rules.
themes: Search/SEO and referral data: Bing/Google keyword volume tools, SERP scrapers, Common Crawl web graph, backlink datasets, AI-bot crawler traffic stats (Cloudflare, Vercel)

name: partially.online
what_it_holds: Real-time internet outage/restriction dashboard aggregating live data from IODA, OONI, and Cloudflare Radar; trinocular Bayesian probing, severity scoring, 30-day country timelines. Not travel/search specific but demonstrates a working multi-source Radar aggregation pipeline.
why_useful: Marginal: could be adapted to flag country-level internet disruptions (which would depress both search demand and STR bookings in a market) as an event/shock indicator, but this is a stretch use of an outage-monitoring tool rather than a direct search/SEO dataset.
time_coverage: rolling 30-day live window, no long history committed
